comment: The reviewed map for scripts/codemods/semantic-colours.ts, run with --map (WS01 step 24: the status colours, the greys, the navy borders and tints, and raw hex colours). Each Tailwind status colour becomes the token of its tone, one token for each shade the pages use (text-emerald-700 becomes text-ok-700), so every class it writes gives exactly the colour of the class it replaces on the plain :root and nothing changes with newLook off; under the new look each shade takes its tone's tint or words from the Looks-3 status tags, but for two that are not tags: the scanner's move marks take mark colours of their own (bg-mark-warn, bg-mark-ok), which stand out from the card, and the checked check-in toggle takes a fixed dark green fill (bg-ok-fill) that keeps its white words at 4.5:1. Every keep entry for a light tone on navy names its own string, so the same class anywhere else is a raw colour. test/unit/semantic-map.test.ts proves it and holds the TSX files to this map, and test/unit/raw-colours.test.ts fails on any raw colour class this map or the step 23 map does not keep and test/unit/fixtures/raw-colours-allowlist.json does not list. Not in this map: StatusBadge's tones (step 26), gold text (text-lca-gold and the gold hex colours, step 25), the announcement banners' red and blue grounds, the Facebook brand blue and the club map's own ground, which stay fixed (the allowlist gives each reason). Club colours are user data and inline styles, so no class carries them. The judgement calls behind the sites and keep entries are recorded under step 24 in REDESIGN_STATUS.md.

rules.reason: Green words on the page, on a card, on a green badge or in a success note. text-ok is emerald-800 with newLook off, and the ok tone's words under the new look (#047857, and #3ecf8e in dark mode).
The lighter green of a check icon or of the Registration open line on a tournament card. Under the new look it is the ok tone's words, which turn light in dark mode.

Green words that report a success on the page (Saved, Sent, every move checked) and the second line of a success note. Emerald-700 is dark green on a dark ground in dark mode, so under the new look it takes the ok tone's words.
The heading of a success note and the words of the member strip on /membership. Under the new look they take the ok tone's words, on the ok tint the note turns to.
The words of the scanner's green move mark. Under the new look they take the ok tone's words, on the ok tint the mark turns to.

The ground of a success note, and of the two light islands step 23 left (the member strip on /membership and the finished-event panel on the manage page). Under the new look it is the ok tint, which turns dark in dark mode, so the ink on the islands stays readable.
The ground of a green badge (Active, Paid, Published, Answered, In progress and the audit log's green entries). Under the new look it is the ok tint, with the ok words on it.

The scanner's mark on a move that was fixed, and its swatch in the legend beside the words. A mark has to stand out from the card the moves sit on, and the ok tint (#e8f5ef) would all but vanish there (1.12:1 on white), so it takes a mark colour of its own: emerald-200 with newLook off, on the light looks emerald-200 lightened just enough for the ok words to reach 4.5:1 on it, and a dark green in dark mode. The swatch still matches the mark.
The line around a success note. Under the new look it is the ok tint, like the note's ground, so the note reads as one tinted box, as the Looks-3 tags do.
The green dot the home page's own StatusDot draws for open registration, beside the event's name. Under the new look it is the ok tone's words colour, which shows on either ground.

A player's check-in toggle when checked: a solid green fill under the white words Present. White on emerald-600 is 3.67:1, so under the new look the fill is the dark green #047857 in every look, dark mode included, where white reaches 5.48:1; a tone shade would turn light green in dark mode under the same white words. Emerald-600 with newLook off.
The line of the same checked toggle, which stays with its fill in every look. Its 50 per cent hover line on the unchecked toggle is kept as it is (see keep).
The check icon beside a chosen player in the US Chess lookup. Green is that lookup's own second green; under the new look it takes the ok tone's words.
The rating and the change link inside the US Chess lookup's found note. Under the new look they take the ok tone's words, on the ok tint the note turns to.
The player's name in the US Chess lookup's found note and the words of its Active badge. Under the new look they take the ok tone's words, on the ok tint.
The ground of the US Chess lookup's found note. Under the new look it is the ok tint, which turns dark in dark mode with the light words on it.

The line around the US Chess lookup's found note. Under the new look it is the ok tint, like the note's ground.
The US Chess ID field's border once a player is chosen, a state shown by the field's line. Under the new look it is the ok tone's words colour, which keeps the line visible on either ground.

The words of a red badge: the audit log's red entries and an expired US Chess membership. Under the new look they take the bad tone's words, on the bad tint.

The words of a blue badge (open and new tickets, the audit log's blue entries, the rated badge on a tournament card) and of the support form's sign-in note. Under the new look they take the info tone's words, the navy of the Looks-3 partner tag.
The ground of the rated badge on a tournament card and of the support form's sign-in note. Under the new look it is the info tint.

The words of the Resolved ticket badge on the support pages and the dashboard, and the rating and score beside each name on the print page's pairing sheet. Under the new look they take the closed tag's words, the muted grey #5b6478 (#9aa6bf in dark mode, on the screen only: a printed page takes the light look, so the sheet prints #5b6478 on the white paper).
The ground of the Resolved ticket badge. Under the new look it is the closed tag's tint, #f7f8fa, and #1a2744 in dark mode.
The line of a selected control filled navy (border-lca-navy bg-brand-navy text-white): it stays with the fill it belongs to, #1a2744 in every look and in dark mode.

A navy line on a light ground: a chosen option, a heading rule, a hover or focus border and the faint borders of chips and notes. It follows the ink, so in dark mode it is a light line on the dark ground rather than navy on navy. With a modifier, the tint is the same in every browser that can mix colours, and the block in src/index.css gives older browsers the tint the old class fell back to.
The ring around the chosen tone in the announcement editor, on a light card. It follows the ink, so it still shows in dark mode.

A faint navy tint behind ink text (section chips, avatars and officer initials, chosen rows and options, support replies, Your registration and the view-only note). As a tint of the ink it lightens the dark ground in dark mode instead of vanishing into it. Tailwind gives a token class with a modifier its token at full strength in a browser that cannot mix colours, so the block in src/index.css gives those browsers the tint bg-brand-navy fell back to. The hero photo's veil (/55) and the navy buttons' hover (/90) stay navy.
The navy tick of a checkbox (the family entry panel, the grade confirmation, the news post form). It follows the ink, so a ticked box shows in dark mode; accent-ink is #1a2744 with newLook off.

The Facebook feed's links (visit the page directly, See all posts on Facebook). #1668d8 is 3.31:1 on the dark surface, so the token keeps it in light mode and gives a lighter Facebook blue, #4599ff, in dark mode and the live look.
The words of the Scheduled tag in the admin list of announcements, in the info banner's blue. Under the new look they take the info tone's words, which turn light in dark mode.

The tint behind the Scheduled tag. It keeps its 15 per cent of the token, and the block in src/index.css gives a browser that cannot mix colours the tint the old class gave. The info banner's own solid blue under white words stays as it is (see the allowlist).
